title: The parallel port registers
covers: The data, status and control registers of the PC parallel printer ports at 0278h, 0378h and 03BCh, and what DOSBox-X does at each.

rows.text: 0278h-027Ah are a parallel printer port, usually LPT1 and sometimes LPT2.
The port may sit at 03BCh, 0278h or 0378h.
0278h is the data port.
0278h is write-only: a write sets the data byte the port holds.
The second port is reached only when parallel2 names a backend; by default it is disabled.
When the printer backend answers it, a write stores the byte and a read returns it, so the port is not write-only.
While the port is disabled a read reaches IO_ReadBlocked and returns 0xFF, and a write stores nothing.
0279h is the status port.
A read of 0279h gives the status; its bit table is P0658 at 03BCh.
0279h is read-only.
The second port is reached only when parallel2 names a backend; by default it is disabled.
With the printer backend, a read of the status port is handed to Read_SR.
With the printer backend, before any printer is created a read of the status gives 0xDF.
027Ah is the control port, readable and writable.
A read of 027Ah gives the control bits back.
A write of 027Ah sets the control bits.
The second port is reached only when parallel2 names a backend; by default it is disabled.
With the printer backend, a read returns 0xE0 ORed with the stored byte, so bits 7-5 read as 1; once a printer exists bit 1 is its autofeed.
0378h-037Ah are a parallel printer port, usually LPT2 and sometimes LPT3.
The port may sit at 03BCh, 0278h or 0378h.
0378h is the data port.
0378h is write-only: a write sets the data byte the port holds.
DOSBox-X makes 0378h its first parallel port, LPT1, with the printer backend.
DOSBox-X numbers 0378h as LPT1, where the document places it usually as LPT2.
A write stores the byte and a read of 0378h returns it, so the port is not write-only.
0379h is the status port.
A read of 0379h gives the status; its bit table is P0658 at 03BCh.
0379h is read-only.
0379h answers by default: parallel1 names the printer backend, whose object installs the LPT1 handlers.
With the printer backend, a read of the status port is handed to Read_SR.
With the printer backend, before any printer is created a read of the status gives 0xDF.
037Ah is the control port, readable and writable.
A read of 037Ah gives the control bits back.
A write of 037Ah sets the control bits.
037Ah answers by default: parallel1 names the printer backend, whose object installs the LPT1 handlers.
With the printer backend, a read of the control port is handed to Read_COM and a write to Write_CON.
With the printer backend, a read returns 0xE0 ORed with the stored byte, so bits 7-5 read as 1; once a printer exists bit 1 is its autofeed.
03BCh-03BFh are the parallel printer port, LPT1 on an MDA.
The port may sit at 0278h, 0378h or 03BCh.
03BCh is the data port.
On a unidirectional port a read of 03BCh gives the last byte written.
On a bidirectional port a read of 03BCh gives input from the connector.
A write of 03BCh sets the data byte the port holds.
The third port is reached only when parallel3 names a backend; by default it is disabled.
The port's read is handed to Read_PR and its write to Write_PR of the printer backend.
With the printer backend, DOSBox-X has no bidirectional data path: a read returns the last byte written.
While the port is disabled a read reaches IO_ReadBlocked and returns 0xFF, and a write stores nothing.
03BDh is the status port.
A read of 03BDh gives the status register.
Bit 7 of the status is busy.
Bit 6 is NOT acknowledge, a pulse about 5 microseconds low.
Bit 5 of the status is out of paper.
Bit 4 is set when the printer is selected.
Bit 3 of the status is the *no* error bit.
Bit 2 is clear when an interrupt has occurred; on a PS/2 it is a printer -ACK.
Bits 1-0 of the status are reserved.
Reading the status sets bit 2 again when an interrupt left it clear.
The third port is reached only when parallel3 names a backend; by default it is disabled.
The status port's read handler is installed at base+1 and no write handler is installed for it.
With the printer backend, before any printer is created a read of the status gives 0xDF.
DOSBox-X sets bit 7 when the printer is not busy, the opposite of the table, and its printer is never busy, so bit 7 stays set.
DOSBox-X returns bits 1-0 set, where the document reserves them.
With the printer backend, bit 6 stays set until a printed byte clears it for one read, not as a 5 microsecond pulse.
With the printer backend, reading the status sets no bit of it: the body returns the value it composed and bit 2 is never set by a read.
03BEh is the control port, readable and writable.
A read of 03BEh gives the control bits back.
Bits 7-6 are stored with the control byte; the document reserves them and defers bit 7 to 037Bh.
Bit 5 is stored; on a PS/2 it enables the bidirectional port, with PORT 0102h.
Bit 4 is stored; it enables the IRQ that -ACK raises.
Bit 3 is stored; it selects the printer on the SLCT IN line.
Bit 2 at 0 initializes the printer on the -RESET line.
Bit 1 is stored and selects the automatic line feed.
The programmer holds bit 0 of the control set for at least 5 microseconds as the strobe.
The third port is reached only when parallel3 names a backend; by default it is disabled.
The control port's handlers are installed at base+2 and handed to Read_COM and Write_CON.
With the printer backend, a read returns 0xE0 ORed with the stored byte, so bits 7-5 read as 1; once a printer exists bit 1 is its autofeed.
DOSBox-X resets the printer when bit 2 rises from 0 to 1, not while it is 0.
DOSBox-X prints the stored data byte when bit 0 falls from 1 to 0.
With the printer backend, bit 4 is stored but no interrupt is raised: the event handler is empty.
